integrity: For two exact prime-power blocks X,Y, the unitary totient is (X-1)(Y-1). Combining this with consecutiveness turns each parity orientation into a difference-of-squares identity with product A-1, where A is the exact power of two in the even member. The three displayed branches are obtained by solving those identities and their converses are checked algebraically. Finite enumeration is corroborative only.
scientific_limitations: The classification assumes that each member of the consecutive pair has exactly two distinct prime divisors. It does not classify higher-support unitary-totient collisions. The exact collision database contains many examples outside this support stratum. An equivalent parametrization may exist in unindexed computational or recreational notes.
title: Mersenne-factor parametrization of consecutive two-support unitary-totient collisions
